name: security-aws-sqs-queue-policy-review
intent: SQS producer/consumer authority and message-driven operations
artifacts: Queue resource/identity policies, sender context, encryption, dead-letter routing and consumer validation.
trace: Trace who can send, receive, delete or redrive messages and whether message body/attributes grant downstream authority.
experiment: Use a small owned queue or local consumer with synthetic messages; compare rightful producer processing and an untrusted actor/authority field.
disproof: A visible queue URL is not queue access; authorized message submission alone is not application privilege escalation.
repair: Constrain queue operations and independently validate the consumer action/resource policy, including redrive.
branch_decisions: Separate send, receive, delete and queue-policy administration. Message attributes are producer-controlled unless another verified envelope binds them. Inspect visibility timeout and redelivery as normal delivery behavior, then check consumer idempotency/authority at the final action. Receiving a test message proves read access only to the tested queue and principal.
operational_method: For SNS/EventBridge/service-to-queue delivery, inspect the queue resource-policy principal and applicable aws:SourceArn/aws:SourceAccount constraints. Match the exact source rather than accepting a payload source label. If SSE-KMS applies, keep KMS denial distinct from queue policy denial. The local fixture should model queue admission before consumer processing and use one source-allowed and one source-mismatched marker; no receive/list access to unrelated queues is needed.
